issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int) and the reference solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in parameters will confuse students and prevents them from implementing or testing the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution by providing public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (remove the boolean parameter), or add an overloaded method addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the validation variant. Ensure the UML, problem text, template, and solution use the same single-parameter signature.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with a different signature (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) than the method described in the problem statement UML and implemented in the solution (addGuestStudents(int)). This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation will confuse students mapping the requirement to the starter code and may cause compilation/tests to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation behavior is desired, either implement it inside that single-parameter method or provide a clearly documented overloaded helper method (e.g. private boolean validateGuestCount(int)) so the public API matches the exercise specification.
